purpose: Prove the Base -> Arc CCTP V2 forwarding path end to end on testnet before any real money is bridged.

route.note: Direction is mirrored relative to production (Base -> Arc) but exercises the identical code path: approve, depositForBurnWithHook, forwarding hook, Iris attestation polling, forwarded mint.

attempts.detail: depositForBurnWithHook reverted with 'ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance'.
attempts.rootCause: On Arc the gas token IS USDC and shares one balance with the ERC-20 interface. The approve transaction consumed gas, so the balance read before it was stale. The script then tried to burn more than the wallet still held.
attempts.fix: Re-read the USDC balance after the approve, estimate the burn transaction's gas, and reserve that (plus a 0.01 USDC margin) before computing the burn amount. Only applies where gas and the bridged token are the same asset.

productionInterfaceCheck.method: eth_call depositForBurnWithHook(5 USDC, domain 26, ...) against the real Base mainnet TokenMessengerV2
productionInterfaceCheck.result: reverted with 'ERC20: transfer amount exceeds allowance'
productionInterfaceCheck.conclusion: The production ABI, selector and argument encoding all decode correctly — execution reached the token transfer, which is exactly the expected failure before an approve.

untestedForProduction: The no-reserve branch (gas is a separate asset on Base) — trivial: the reserve is simply zero.
Live iteration against a real production Iris message — the endpoint and response shape were verified with direct calls.
